DeepWalk generates truncated random walks and feeds them to a skip-gram model, so its window size and walk length let it capture deeper, multi-hop neighborhood structure, and it is flexible in how far it looks. LINE explicitly models only first-order proximity (directly connected nodes) and second-order proximity (nodes sharing neighbors), so it explores shallower neighborhoods but with a fixed, explicit objective. The trade-off is between depth and flexibility on one side and efficiency and explicit control on the other: DeepWalk reaches deeper, more global structure at higher sampling cost and with less direct control over what is preserved, while LINE is cheaper and more interpretable but limited to a fixed, shallow neighborhood scope.
